root_cause_label: Agent created a qcow2 disk instead of raw, launched QEMU with no unattended installation setup (no winnt.sif, no product key injection, no tb-admin automation), then claimed completion based solely on service liveness without ever verifying Windows XP reached the login screen.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent created the VM disk in qcow2 format (not raw), booted QEMU from CD without any unattended installation mechanism, and issued a placeholder completion marker without verifying that Windows XP had installed, booted to the login screen, or that the tb-admin account existed.
t_commit_evidence: Step 9: QEMU launched (`qemu-system-i386 -drive file=/app/isos/xp.img,format=qcow2 -cdrom /app/isos/xp.iso ... -vnc :1 -daemonize`) with the qcow2 disk and no unattended installation configuration; from this point the agent pivots entirely to service-liveness checks and never revisits the core installation problem, locking in the failure outcome.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked domain knowledge of two critical requirements: (1) that Windows XP installation in a headless QEMU environment requires an unattended answer file (winnt.sif) with the product key and account names injected into the ISO before booting, and (2) that the benchmark expected a raw disk image rather than qcow2. The agent correctly retrieved the product key but never understood how to use it in an unattended fashion.
